cohort: The study included 20 pregnant patients who underwent percutaneous nephrostomy placement over a 12-year period.
finding: Percutaneous nephrostomy placement demonstrates good clinical results as a treatment option for ureteral obstruction in pregnant patients, with high technical success and reported maternal and fetal outcomes.
mod_finding: Emergency C-sections were required in two out of 20 cases.
followup_time: Until time of delivery (for fetal outcomes); median 82 days for catheter in situ.
